plates.title: Spider Silk: From Biology to Imitation
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page in aged parchment tones, ink line work with muted gold, green and rust pigment washes, bordered by thin vine-scroll filigree but with a wide clear central field. Down the page, in reading order, place fifteen framed vignettes connected by thin ribbon-lines flowing top to bottom, branching where noted: a spider at web-centre spinning several threads (ONE SILK, MANY THREADS); a stone archway strand under tension (STRONG AND STRETCHY); a cross-section of thread with crystal blocks in soft mesh (CRYSTALS IN A SOFT WEB); a thread bending under a falling weight (ABSORBING THE FALL); a tiny glued rosette disc on a leaf (GLUE THAT SETS AT ONCE); a spider with seven thread-spools (SEVEN KINDS OF THREAD); an orb web with bold rim and spokes, spider dangling (THE DRAGLINE RIM); a spider's rear drawing out a hardening thread (PULLED, NOT PUMPED); a scholar's bench with vial and duct (COPYING PROTEIN AND DUCT); a flask of bacteria beside spun thread (BACTERIA-MADE SILK); a hand pressing a syringe spinning thread (SYRINGE SPINNING); tiny spheres and a woven patch near a bandaged wound (CAPSULES AND SCAFFOLDS); two threads compared, dull thick vs fine gleaming (STILL SHORT OF THE SPIDER); a scholar with radiating-line instrument over thread (MAPPING THE THREAD); stockings and gloves woven from golden thread (STOCKINGS FROM COCOONS). Group the properties vignettes and synthesis vignettes each inside faint dashed enclosures labeled only by their framing line, no words. No lettering anywhere except the vignette titles in careful capitals beneath each scene.

plates.title: Inside Properties
plates.prompt: Illuminated manuscript register matching the overview page: parchment ground, ink linework, muted gold-green-rust washes, thin filigree border, clear central field. At the top, a woven lattice panel with hard faceted blocks threaded through soft coils (HARD BLOCKS, SOFT COILS), feeding a ribbon-line down into a central hub scene: a thread bowing deeply to catch a falling stone (CATCHING THE FALL). From this hub, five ribbon-lines fan outward to framed vignettes arranged in a loose arc below: a thread looping softly beside a rigid unbending rod (BENDS WHERE STEEL WON'T); a single thread holding aloft a heavy iron weight (STRONG AS STEEL); a slender thread looped entirely around a small drawn globe (A THREAD AROUND THE WORLD); a spider thread and a woven fabric swatch shown side by side under equal strain (MATCHING THE BEST FIBRE); and a dew-wet web with visibly shortened, curling threads (SHRINKING IN THE DEW). From the globe vignette, one ribbon-line descends further to a final scene at the page's foot: a small sealed attachment disc on a twig, dissolving at its edges into the bark (GLUE THAT FADES AWAY). Keep the composition filling the width of the page, each scene large enough to read clearly, with generous bare parchment rather than clutter. No lettering anywhere except the vignette titles in careful capitals beneath each scene.

plates.title: Inside Artificial Synthesis
plates.prompt: Illuminated manuscript register matching the earlier pages: parchment ground, ink linework, muted gold-green-rust washes, thin filigree border, clear wide central field. At the top, a scholar's bench split in two, vial of protein on the left and small mechanical duct on the right (TWO TASKS, ONE BENCH), with two ribbon-lines descending to form two columns. Left column, headed by a small menagerie of labelled-by-shape jars: bacterium flask, silkworm cocoon, goat (BORROWED CREATURES), branching to a flask of bacteria beside a thread matched against a natural one (BACTERIA MATCHING SPIDER) and a goat being milked with fine thread spun beside the pail (SILK FROM GOAT'S MILK). Right column, headed by a droplet entering a maze-like tapering tube (A MAZE FOR THE LIQUID), branching to a hand with a syringe dripping thread into a basin of liquid (HARDENING WITH CHEMICALS) and a channeled device spooling continuous thread onto a reel (A CONTINUOUS SPOOL). Both columns' ribbon-lines converge at the bottom into one final scene: a hand holding up all the gathered threads for comparison against a natural web (STILL FALLING SHORT). Keep scenes large and legible, filling the page's width as well as height, with generous bare parchment rather than crowding. No lettering anywhere except the vignette titles in careful capitals beneath each scene.

vignettes.quote: Various organisms have been used as a basis for attempts to replicate necessary protein components

vignettes.quote: having similar mechanical characteristics as their natural counterparts
